name: UTF-8 HEX Encoder
summary: Encode Unicode text into contiguous lowercase hexadecimal pairs representing its exact UTF-8 bytes.
inputParameters: Unicode text encoded by the browser TextEncoder
outputFormats: Lowercase hexadecimal with two digits per UTF-8 byte
useCases: Inspect the UTF-8 bytes behind a short string
Prepare a byte-level text fixture for debugging

limitations: The result represents UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units or an integer value.
No separators or 0x prefixes are emitted.
The engine accepts text rather than original binary file bytes.

name: Strict UTF-8 HEX Decoder
summary: Decode complete hexadecimal byte pairs into text only when the resulting byte sequence is valid UTF-8.
inputParameters: Even-length hexadecimal byte pairs with optional whitespace
useCases: Recover text from a UTF-8 HEX fixture
Detect invalid UTF-8 byte sequences during debugging

limitations: Odd-length input and non-hexadecimal characters are rejected.
Byte sequences invalid under strict UTF-8 decoding are rejected rather than replaced.
The engine is not a general binary file viewer.

name: Unicode Code Point Inspector
summary: List each iterated Unicode code point with hexadecimal notation, decimal value, and UTF-16 unit length.
inputParameters: Unicode text iterated by JavaScript string code points
outputFormats: JSON array of character and code-point records
useCases: Distinguish supplementary characters from single UTF-16 units
Inspect invisible or unfamiliar characters in copied text
searchIntents: character to U plus code locally

limitations: Indexes count iterated code points rather than UTF-16 offsets.
Combining sequences and joined emoji can span multiple records despite appearing as one grapheme.
The engine does not resolve Unicode names, scripts, normalization forms, or confusable characters.

name: ROT13 Text Transformer
summary: Apply the self-inverse ROT13 substitution to ASCII letters while leaving all other characters unchanged.
outputFormats: Text with A-Z and a-z rotated by thirteen positions
useCases: Decode legacy ROT13 discussion text
Demonstrate a reversible substitution transform

limitations: Only ASCII letters are transformed.
ROT13 provides no confidentiality, authentication, or modern cryptographic protection.
Applying the engine twice restores the original ASCII letters.

name: Whitespace Normalizer
summary: Trim surrounding whitespace and collapse every internal whitespace run into one ordinary space character.
inputParameters: Text containing spaces, tabs, newlines, or other JavaScript whitespace
useCases: Clean copied prose for a one-line field
Normalize whitespace before an exact text comparison

limitations: All line boundaries are destroyed.
Whitespace inside code, quoted data, or significant formatting is also collapsed.
The engine does not apply language-aware punctuation spacing.

name: Empty Line Remover
summary: Remove blank and whitespace-only lines while preserving the exact content of every remaining line.
inputParameters: Multiline text using LF, CRLF, or CR line endings
outputFormats: Non-empty lines joined with LF characters
useCases: Clean spacing from a pasted identifier list
Remove blank rows from a simple text export

limitations: Whitespace on retained lines is not trimmed.
All output line endings become LF.
Removing blank lines can change meaning in code, Markdown, configuration, and paragraph-oriented text.

name: Line Order Reverser
summary: Reverse the order of normalized text lines without reversing characters inside the individual lines.
inputParameters: Multiline text using LF, CRLF, or CR line endings
outputFormats: Lines in reverse order joined with LF characters
useCases: Flip a chronological line list
Inspect a log excerpt from last line to first

limitations: Characters inside lines remain unchanged.
Output line endings are normalized to LF.
Leading or trailing empty lines participate in the reversal.

name: Email Candidate Extractor
summary: Extract unique email-shaped strings using a practical case-sensitive pattern intended for text discovery rather than validation.
inputParameters: Text potentially containing conventional email-shaped strings
outputFormats: Unique candidates in first-seen order, one per line
useCases: Find contact candidates in an authorized document
Review email-shaped values in a test fixture
searchIntents: find emails in text without upload

limitations: A regex match does not prove mailbox existence or full standards validity.
Deduplication is case-sensitive.
Internationalized domains, quoted local parts, comments, and uncommon valid address forms may not match.

name: HTTP URL Candidate Extractor
summary: Extract unique HTTP and HTTPS URL-shaped strings and trim selected punctuation commonly attached in prose.
inputParameters: Text containing absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL candidates
outputFormats: Unique URL candidates in first-seen order, one per line
useCases: Collect links from an authorized text export
Inspect HTTP references embedded in logs or notes
searchIntents: find HTTPS links in text browser

limitations: Only absolute HTTP and HTTPS candidates are considered.
Extraction does not fetch, resolve, validate, or classify the URLs.
Heuristic trailing-punctuation removal can be imperfect when punctuation is legitimately part of a URL.

name: Arbitrary-Precision Integer Base Converter
summary: Convert signed whole numbers between bases 2 and 36 using JavaScript BigInt without floating-point precision loss.
inputParameters: Integer digits, source base, and target base separated by whitespace
useCases: Convert binary or hexadecimal identifiers to decimal
Check large integer representations without Number precision loss

limitations: Only signed integers are accepted; fractional values and scientific notation are rejected.
Bases are limited to integers from 2 through 36.
Output letters use uppercase and no radix prefix is added.
